newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Greek Cypriot students protest along 'green line'.
newsitem.headline: Greek Cypriot students protest along 'green line'.

text.p: Groups of Greek Cypriot students demonstrated along the "green line" dividing the capital Nicosia on Tuesday, shortly before the scheduled funeral of a man shot dead by Turkish Cypriot troops on Sunday.

Secondary school students gathered at the United Nations- controlled Ledra Palace checkpoint chanting "Our borders are in Kyrenia" but quickly dispersed. Other students held protests in schoolyards. Some 200 to 300 took part in total.
Kyrenia, on the north coast of Cyprus, has been occupied by Turkish forces since 1974 when Turkey invaded the northern third of the island in response to a Greek-engineered coup in Nicosia.
Retired Greek Cypriot fireman Petros Kakouli, 58, is due to be buried in the southeast village of Avgorou later on Tuesday.

Turkish Cypriot troops shot him dead when he entered Turkish-occupied territory on Sunday morning. His family said he was in the area collecting snails. Turkish forces said he failed to stop when ordered to by troops and was shot whilst escaping.

The incident, which the United Nations peacekeeping force on the island described as "deplorable", happened near the eastern end of the buffer zone, close to Achna village and territory controlled by British military bases.
Cypriot Finance Minister Christodoulos Christodoulou and Greece's minister for the Aegean, Elisavet Papazoi, are expected to attend the funeral.
U.N. officials said security has been stepped up along the buffer zone dividing the island.
"The order is to be extremely vigilant," U.N. spokesman Waldemar Rokoszewski said.
Four Greek Cypriots and one Turkish Cypriot have been killed along the buffer zone since June.
A Turkish Cypriot breakaway state in the north, recognised only by Ankara, was established in 1983.
